sections.what_happened: Iraqi oil exports averaged >3.4M bpd so far in October (ministry: ~3.0M in Sept; OilPrice: 2.65M Sept; +~750k bpd), approaching the 3.3-3.5M pre-war level. Three routes: Strait of Hormuz (most crude still via Basra), Turkey's Ceyhan port (250k bpd Sept), tanker trucks through Syria (first trucks expected at Mediterranean port mid-Oct). State Oil Tankers Company shipped 2M bbl through Hormuz on its own VLCC — first in decades; SOMO in talks to buy its own tankers. Recovery follows collapse: exports plunged from >99M bbl in Feb to 18.6M bbl in March; FM Fuad Hussein: $60B losses, reserves -$20B, dinar devalued (first in 3+ years). Oil = ~90% of government revenue. Context: US Energy Sec Chris Wright (Fox): Gulf flows at ~80% of prewar; ~1,600 'dark fleet' vessels; US authorizing sale of sanctioned tankers to expand legal shipping capacity.
sections.what_verified: OilPrice, Rudaw, Straits Times, Iraq Business News, europesays — consistent figures and three-route detail.
sections.what_disputed: Figures are Iraqi-government claims via INA; independent Kpler/tanker-tracking confirmation not seen in-window (note: 0600-02 Kpler data showed regional flows depressed — reconcile before long-form use). Sept figure discrepancy (3.0M ministry vs 2.65M OilPrice) noted.
sections.why_matters: Hard data on the Hormuz war's economics: Iraq is back near pre-war export levels through three routes. Map the three routes on screen — this is the 'blockade vs counter-blockade' scoreboard. TOTW stance: present Iraqi figures as government claims; the dark-fleet/Wright context shows Washington's workaround layer.
